query: For high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles intended for catalysis, sensing, energy storage, corrosion-related uses, and other applications requiring thermal stability, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs their premelting and melting behavior and why? Specify a controlled comparison that would reveal the governing factor, the observations expected relative to a baseline, the range over which the hypothesis should hold, prior evidence that supports it, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Surface segregation of low‐melting‐point elements in high‐entropy‐alloy nanoparticles controls the onset of premelting and reduces the overall melting temperature by weakening surface lattice cohesion.
generation.material_initial_state: As‐synthesized HEA nanoparticles (5–20 nm) with a random solid‐solution composition.
generation.intervention: Thermally anneal one batch at a subsolidus temperature to promote enrichment of the lowest‐melting‐point element at the surface; quench a control batch to retain uniform composition.
generation.conditions: Inert‐atmosphere in situ heating (e.g. TEM or DSC), heating rate ~10 K/min, temperature range from 300 K up to complete melting.
generation.structural_mediator: Surface concentration profile of the low‐melting‐point element (e.g. measured by STEM‐EDS line scans).
generation.mechanism: Segregated surface sites have reduced atomic coordination and weaker bonding, initiating premelting at lower temperatures and propagating inward.
generation.predicted_outcome: Annealed (segregated) nanoparticles exhibit onset of surface premelting and bulk melting 50–100 K below the uniform‐composition baseline.
generation.baseline: Uniform‐composition HEA nanoparticles without induced segregation.
generation.boundary: Holds for 5–20 nm HEA nanoparticles composed of elements whose individual melting points differ by ≥200 K, under inert or vacuum conditions.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate: kinetic barriers to segregation and measurement precision may shift observed ΔT by ±20 K.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two HEA nanoparticle batches: (1) annealed at T_a (~0.7 T_mix) for surface segregation; (2) quenched to freeze uniform composition. Perform in situ TEM heating and DSC on both.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If annealed and quenched batches differ in onset or melting temperature by <20 K, the hypothesis is falsified.
